TIPTAP FOR BUBBLE The most flexible and complete Rich Text Editor for Bubble. From a simple input field to a fully fledged Google Docs or Notions type of experience. This plugin can do it all. 55+ actions  •  HTML / JSON / text  •  Autobinding  •  Tables & images  •  Live collab Type, format, and watch Bubble states. Select text to format it. To add an emoji, place the cursor in the editor and type :smile: or click Insert emoji. The buttons are Bubble workflows, and the readout shows Bubble states you can save to a Thing. No picker is included. Bold Italic H2 Bullet list Highlight Insert emoji Welcome to Tiptap This is a real Tiptap editor on a Bubble page. Select this sentence and click Bold — that button is an ordinary Bubble workflow calling a Tiptap element action. What you can type Headings, lists, and checklists Tables you can tab through Images you drop onto the page Emoji: type :smile: to turn it into an inline node Markdown shortcuts work too. Type # then space for a heading, or - then space for a bullet list. A small table State What you do with it Content (HTML) Save it to a Thing Character count Show a limit Is focused Style a wrapper The readout below is the same Bubble states you would use in your own app. ⠿ BUBBLE STATES Character count: 621 Word count: 121 Is focused: Is empty: no Can undo: no Can redo: no Selection is bold: no Selection is italic: no Selected text: How you would wire this in your app. 1. Drop a Tiptap element on the page. 2. Give it initial content — HTML or plain text. 3. Save This Tiptap's Content (HTML) to a Thing, or turn on autobinding. 4. Build your own toolbar with element actions. The buttons above also include Insert emoji, which adds a named emoji at the cursor. Turn on Emoji for shortcode and Unicode conversion. Type :smile: or use Insert emoji with the name smile. There is no built-in picker. Markdown shortcuts still work: # for H1, - for a bullet list, [] for a task. A table of contents that follows your document. Scroll inside the editor and watch the active item move through the separate Table of Contents element. Edit any heading and the outline updates from the editor’s Bubble state. Product guide Scroll inside this editor and watch the active item in the outline below. This document starts at H2 on purpose, so an H1 is not required. The content is long enough to show how the outline follows a real article, help center page, or internal document. Plan the document Start with the questions your reader needs answered. Group related details into sections that are easy to scan. Use headings for structure rather than appearance. A clear outline helps readers understand where they are and what comes next. Keep the most important sections near the top, then move supporting detail into smaller subsections. Name sections clearly Prefer short labels that describe the outcome, such as Configure the editor or Publish the article. The same labels appear in the table of contents, so they should still make sense without the paragraphs around them. Configure the editor Add the Tiptap editor to a Group with a fixed height. Turn on overflow scrolling for that Group when the document should stay inside a compact panel. The editor can also grow with the page. Choose the layout that matches the reading experience in your app. Initial content can come from plain text, HTML, Tiptap JSON, or a field on a Bubble Thing. Enable the outline Turn on the Table of contents extension and Unique ID. The editor then publishes its Table of contents (JSON) state. Headings can begin at H2, H3, or another level. The visual outline normalizes them into a readable hierarchy. Bind the live outline Add the Tiptap Table of Contents visual element outside the editor’s scroll frame. Set its Table of contents JSON field to this editor’s Table of contents (JSON) state. No custom JavaScript is required. As the reader scrolls, the active and scrolled-over states update automatically. Style active sections Choose normal, scrolled-over, and active colors. You can also control indentation, item spacing, font weight, and the active indicator. Use enough contrast to make the current section clear without distracting from the document. Replace content safely You can load another Thing through Initial content, auto-binding, or the Set Content action. The editor republishes the outline when the document changes, and the visual element replaces stale headings. This makes the same editor and outline reusable across articles, records, and URL-driven pages. Test the experience Scroll from the first section to the last. Check that the active item follows the document and that clicking an outline item reaches the correct heading. Also test documents with no H1, skipped heading levels, and content that changes without a full page reload. On mobile, keep tap targets comfortable and confirm that the editor does not introduce horizontal overflow. Ship an accessible navigation Give the outline a useful accessible label such as On this page. The visual element renders semantic navigation and links. Readers can now scan, scroll, and jump through a long document without losing their place. ⠿ LIVE TABLE OF CONTENTS Product guide Plan the document Name sections clearly Configure the editor Enable the outline Bind the live outline Style active sections Replace content safely Test the experience Ship an accessible navigation How you would wire this in your app. 1. Turn on Table of contents in the Tiptap element. 2. Add the Tiptap Table of Contents visual element. 3. Set its Table of contents JSON field to the editor’s Table of contents (JSON) state. The outline refreshes when headings are edited or the editor loads different content. Documents can start at H2–H6; they do not need an H1. Google Docs experience Material icons, Bubble workflows. How you would wire this. 1. Put Tiptap on the page. 2. Add Bubble buttons. 3. Each button: when clicked → Tiptap action (Bold, H2, …). 4. Each button condition: This Tiptap's selection is bold (or H1, list, …) is true → change background. Copy this reusable. The workflows come with it. A Notion-like editor. Bubble menu on selection, floating menu on empty lines, drag handle on blocks. The menus are Bubble groups. Tiptap only needs their unique IDs. Project notes Select this sentence for the bubble menu. Click the empty line above for the floating menu. Hover the left edge of a block for the drag handle. Do next ⠿ How you would wire this. 1. Draw two groups. Set unique ID to e.g. notionBubbleMenu and notionFloatingMenu. 2. Put buttons in those groups. Wire them to Tiptap actions. 3. On Tiptap, set Bubble menu / Floating menu to those IDs. 4. Turn on Drag Handle. Copy this reusable. Keep the unique IDs unique if you put two editors on one page. Mentions from any Bubble list. Type @. The dropdown is a Search for Users. After you copy the page, bind Data source, Type of content, Label, and ID to your own list. Standup Type @ to mention a teammate. Mentions are a Tiptap extension plus a Bubble data source — not a custom dropdown you have to build. Workflow: When Mentions editor Mention created Mention created fired: 0 times Last mention: How you would wire this. 1. Enable Mention on the Tiptap element. 2. Data source: Search for Users (or any list). 3. Type of content: User. 4. Label: Name. ID: unique id. 5. Trigger character defaults to @. 6. To notify someone, add a workflow: When Tiptap Mention created. Use Created mention ID to find the User and Created mention label in the message. This page does that: the box above counts each mention and shows the last one. Mention created fires once per person picked from the list. Pasting, undo/redo, loading saved content, and edits by other collaborators do not fire it. This app already has users named Rico, Captain Apollo, and Lieutenant Starbuck. Math formulas with LaTeX. Type $$x^2$$ for a formula inside a sentence, or $$$x^2$$$ on an empty line for a formula on its own line. Prices like $5 stay text. Click a formula to edit it in a Bubble popup. Insert inline formula Insert block formula The area of a circle is 𝜋 𝑟 2 πr 2 . Click the formula to edit it. ∑ 𝑖 = 1 𝑛 𝑖 = 𝑛 ( 𝑛 + 1 ) 2 i=1 ∑ n ​ i= 2 n(n+1) ​ A ticket costs $5 or $10. That stays text. States: Selected math type and Selected math LaTeX Selected formula:   How you would wire this. 1. Turn on Mathematics on the Tiptap element (Extensions > Mathematics). 2. Buttons: Insert inline math or Insert block math with the LaTeX, without dollar signs. 3. Editing: add a workflow When Tiptap Math clicked → Reset the popup → Show the popup. The popup's input starts with Selected math LaTeX. 4. Save runs Update math with the input's value. Delete runs Delete math. Both change the formula the user clicked. Formulas are saved in the HTML with their LaTeX, so they load again. Outside the editor (an HTML element, an email) the LaTeX shows as text. Invalid LaTeX shows in red and still saves. In a read-only editor, clicking a formula does nothing. Two reusables. Two skins. No CSS leak. Each Tiptap injects CSS under its own #tiptapEditor-… id. A dark reusable and a light reusable can sit on the same page. Light note Warm paper, serif body. This reusable has its own CSS overrides. Styles stay inside this editor. Dark note Slate background, light type. Same plugin instance type, different CSS overrides. Nothing here leaks into the light note. How you would wire this. 1. Copy the reusables tiptap-light-note and tiptap-dark-note. 2. Drop both on a page. 3. Edit CSS overrides on each Tiptap (paragraph, headings, links, blockquote, background). You do not need a page HTML header to isolate styles. Tiptap in a Bubble popup. Same element, same actions, same states — inside Show/Hide popup workflows. Write a comment How you would wire this. 1. Add a Popup. Put Tiptap inside it. 2. Button → Show the popup. 3. Close → Hide the popup. Copy this reusable. Popups copy with the page. Let the page grow, or scroll inside the editor. Product guide

Scroll inside this editor and watch the active item in the outline below. This document starts at H2 on purpose, so an H1 is not required.

The content is long enough to show how the outline follows a real article, help center page, or internal document.

Plan the document

Start with the questions your reader needs answered. Group related details into sections that are easy to scan.

Use headings for structure rather than appearance. A clear outline helps readers understand where they are and what comes next.

Keep the most important sections near the top, then move supporting detail into smaller subsections.

Name sections clearly

Prefer short labels that describe the outcome, such as Configure the editor or Publish the article.

The same labels appear in the table of contents, so they should still make sense without the paragraphs around them.

Configure the editor

Add the Tiptap editor to a Group with a fixed height. Turn on overflow scrolling for that Group when the document should stay inside a compact panel.

The editor can also grow with the page. Choose the layout that matches the reading experience in your app.

Initial content can come from plain text, HTML, Tiptap JSON, or a field on a Bubble Thing.

Enable the outline

Turn on the Table of contents extension and Unique ID. The editor then publishes its Table of contents (JSON) state.

Headings can begin at H2, H3, or another level. The visual outline normalizes them into a readable hierarchy.

Bind the live outline

Add the Tiptap Table of Contents visual element outside the editor’s scroll frame.

Set its Table of contents JSON field to this editor’s Table of contents (JSON) state. No custom JavaScript is required.

As the reader scrolls, the active and scrolled-over states update automatically.

Style active sections

Choose normal, scrolled-over, and active colors. You can also control indentation, item spacing, font weight, and the active indicator.

Use enough contrast to make the current section clear without distracting from the document.

Replace content safely

You can load another Thing through Initial content, auto-binding, or the Set Content action.

The editor republishes the outline when the document changes, and the visual element replaces stale headings.

This makes the same editor and outline reusable across articles, records, and URL-driven pages.

Test the experience

Scroll from the first section to the last. Check that the active item follows the document and that clicking an outline item reaches the correct heading.

Also test documents with no H1, skipped heading levels, and content that changes without a full page reload.

On mobile, keep tap targets comfortable and confirm that the editor does not introduce horizontal overflow.

Ship an accessible navigation

Give the outline a useful accessible label such as On this page. The visual element renders semantic navigation and links.

Readers can now scan, scroll, and jump through a long document without losing their place.
